## Accepted scalar cohort and computational dimensions

All nine warehouse-only scalar observations meet the 1% global-gap target and pass independent feasibility validation. The original h500 result extends the reported sequence to 500 facilities. Two separate h215 D observations bring the Gurobi cohort to eleven; they are distinct configurations rather than eleven independent replications.

All five h300 objectives and best bounds coincide; their original warehouse, flow, inventory and shortage CSVs are byte-identical across arms. Native Runtime ranges from 47.14 to 67.61 minutes and sampled application RSS from 46.35 to 78.37 GiB. This establishes identical exported vectors in this block, not a unique optimum.

@fig-scalar-threads compares the observed runtime and sampled memory for these five configurations.

![Thread-count observations at 300 sites.](figures/scalar_threads.png){#fig-scalar-threads fig-pos="H"}

The single-thread observation has the lowest recorded runtime and memory in this block. The five configurations returned identical exported plans; the observations describe this execution sequence rather than a replicated estimate of parallel speedup.

: Investment quantities. The bulkification basis determines handling-rate gains; it is not additional static storage. {#tbl-scalar-quantities}

All included candidates are activated and receive positive capacity through h500. The h500 aggregate records 354 candidate investments, 72 positive expansions and 74 positive bulk conversions. The original h215–h400 vector audits additionally establish positive transport at every included warehouse and nine used export roles; those two geographic-use findings are not extrapolated to the h500 aggregate. These are returned plan characteristics, not uniqueness or infrastructure feasibility.

|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| h215 DET | 91.8612 | 55.1578 | 77.8448 | 57.3404 |

: Physical diagnostics over the declared horizon. STO quantities are probability-weighted, not unweighted sums over nine scenarios. {#tbl-scalar-physical}

Across the returned STO plans, additional candidate sites accompany more installed candidate capacity and greater one-time investment, while the transport and holding components are lower. This is a descriptive comparison of separately screened models and feasible incumbents, not a causal savings estimate. Domestic service is not monotone across populations. Lower stock and reception exceedances can coexist with substantial unmet demand; a lower penalized total is not improvement in every service component.

### Geographic interpretation

@fig-map-h215, @fig-map-h300 and @fig-map-h400 locate the facilities and investments in the returned stochastic plans. Origin products and domestic/export destinations are distinguished. Coincident facilities retain their original identities.

![Stochastic plan at 215 warehouse sites.](figures/scalar_h215_sto.png){#fig-map-h215 fig-pos="H"}

The 215-site map shows the spatial distribution of the returned investment decisions. The accompanying capacity and service tables quantify their consequences. The screened networks differ across populations, so the map is interpreted together with those model-specific results.

![Stochastic plan at 300 warehouse sites.](figures/scalar_h300_t1.png){#fig-map-h300 fig-pos="H"}

The 300-site map shows the spatial distribution of the returned investment decisions. The accompanying capacity and service tables quantify their consequences. The screened networks differ across populations, so the map is interpreted together with those model-specific results.

![Stochastic plan at 400 warehouse sites.](figures/scalar_h400_t1.png){#fig-map-h400 fig-pos="H"}

The 400-site map shows the spatial distribution of the returned investment decisions. The accompanying capacity and service tables quantify their consequences. The screened networks differ across populations, so the map is interpreted together with those model-specific results.

@fig-map-h500 shows the investments reconstructed from the original accepted h500 decision vector.

![Stochastic investments at 500 warehouse sites.](figures/scalar_h500_t1.png){#fig-map-h500 fig-pos="H"}

The original h500 vector assigns positive capacity to all 354 candidates, expands 72 existing sites and converts 74 for bulk handling. These location decisions do not establish equal operational importance or use. The companion capacity maps use circle area to show added candidate and expansion storage in tonnes, excluding bulk-handling investment basis. Road polylines are unavailable for these maps, so the geographic views contain no connecting flow segments.

The local read-only dashboard provides the corresponding DET/STO, population, incremental-membership, product, period and scenario filters, preserving coincident identifiers. Its ability to display a flow requires original positive-flow evidence and source-bound road geometry. Geography alone is not a validation of the agricultural plan.
